reference.source: ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis guidance and respiratory genetics texts
clinicalPearls: Suspect a heritable cause when pulmonary fibrosis occurs in two or more relatives, or at a young age
Telomere-related genes (for example TERT, TERC, RTEL1, PARN) are the commonest identifiable cause, and surfactant genes (SFTPC, SFTPA2) also contribute
A telomere biology disorder may reveal itself through extrapulmonary clues such as early greying of hair, unexplained cytopenias, or cryptogenic liver disease
Inheritance is usually autosomal dominant with incomplete penetrance, so an apparently unaffected parent can still carry the variant
High-resolution imaging and histology often show a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern, but other patterns occur
Genetic counselling and consideration of testing are important because results influence family screening and transplant planning
Patients with short telomeres may tolerate immunosuppression poorly and are prone to marrow and hepatic complications after transplantation
reference.pathophysiology: Familial pulmonary fibrosis arises when inherited variants impair the maintenance of alveolar epithelial cells. Mutations in telomere maintenance genes lead to critically short telomeres and premature senescence of type II pneumocytes, while surfactant gene mutations cause misfolded protein accumulation and epithelial cell stress. In genetically susceptible lungs, repeated alveolar epithelial injury triggers aberrant wound healing with fibroblast activation and progressive deposition of extracellular matrix, producing irreversible scarring and loss of functioning lung.
additionalDifferentials: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease
additionalInvestigations: High-resolution chest computed tomography to define the fibrosis pattern
Genetic testing for telomere-related and surfactant genes
Telomere length measurement in blood leucocytes
Full blood count and liver function tests to screen for telomere-related marrow and hepatic disease
Autoimmune serology to exclude connective tissue disease
Pulmonary function tests with gas transfer and, when needed, multidisciplinary review of histology
redFlags: Rapidly progressive breathlessness or an acute exacerbation of fibrosis
Unexplained cytopenias or bone marrow failure suggesting a telomere disorder
Cryptogenic cirrhosis or portal hypertension in a patient with lung fibrosis
Resting or exertional hypoxaemia indicating advanced disease
reference.prognosis: Familial pulmonary fibrosis is generally progressive and often carries a poor prognosis similar to or worse than sporadic idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; telomere-related disease may progress faster and complicate transplantation, though antifibrotic therapy can slow decline in appropriate patients.
pitfalls: Missing the diagnosis because a detailed family history was not taken
Giving high-dose immunosuppression to patients with short telomeres, which can precipitate marrow failure
Attributing cytopenias or liver disease to unrelated causes rather than a unifying telomere disorder
Failing to offer genetic counselling and family screening
references: ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT clinical practice guideline on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
Standard respiratory medicine and genetics texts
management: Offer antifibrotic therapy with pirfenidone or nintedanib to slow decline in progressive fibrosing, usual-interstitial-pneumonia-pattern disease
Use immunosuppression with caution and generally avoid it where a telomere biology disorder is identified, as it can be harmful in this context
Provide supportive care with supplemental oxygen for hypoxaemia, pulmonary rehabilitation and vaccination
Screen for and monitor extrapulmonary telomere-related complications such as cytopenias and cryptogenic liver disease
Refer early for lung transplantation assessment, recognising that telomere-related disease affects marrow and hepatic reserve and complicates peri-transplant management
Review within an interstitial lung disease multidisciplinary team integrating imaging, histology and genetics
Offer genetic counselling and testing for telomere-related and surfactant genes to guide family screening and transplant planning
